heroHeadline: Senate Passes HOPE/HELP Trade Extension; Port-au-Prince Holds First Criminal Assizes Since 2018; Germany Offers GSF Airlift Support
heroSubtitle: In a rare run of institutional developments, the US Senate approved a two-year extension of Haiti's HOPE/HELP duty-free trade programs on August 11, 2026 — a bipartisan measure championed by Sen. Raphael Warnock that still needs a second House vote in September before reaching President Trump's desk, but offers a lifeline to Haiti's garment-export sector after the programs lapsed in September 2025. On August 13, Port-au-Prince's criminal court convened Assizes jury-trial proceedings for the first time since 2018, with BINUH support, aimed at easing chronic pretrial detention and prison overcrowding. Germany's Bundeswehr offered airlift capacity on August 17 to help ferry equipment and troops for Gang Suppression Force contributing nations (Chad, Sri Lanka, Mongolia, Bangladesh, Guatemala, Côte d'Ivoire), whose advance force remains around 1,000 of the 5,550-person authorized ceiling per the July 20 UN Security Council briefing. GSF Commander Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri visited Artibonite on August 13 to assess the newly arrived Sri Lankan contingent in Gonaïves, a department that recorded 381 killings — 25.7% of Haiti's 2026 national total. Opposition figure André Michel publicly demanded restored security and unblocked highways ahead of the December 13 elections, registering to vote himself on August 17. Inflation continued easing to 18.9% in June 2026, down from 20.0% in May. The underlying security crisis remains dire and unresolved: the UN documented 613 killed and 375 injured between March 6 and July 31, 2026 in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cité Soleil areas alone, part of the wave of attacks (Kenscoff, Gros-Mornes, Arcahaie) reported August 7–9 that continues to cloud the security outlook for December's vote.
